summary: A target-level continuation of T.1: import the existing graded-map and degree-three nodes, specify their full generator, grading, naturality and uniqueness interfaces, and promote the degree-two comparison to its own target. The source-reading part of G-product-symbol is completed with Weibel and Loday; the actual product-model and sign compatibility remains an explicit K.7 supplier request. V.2 consumes the degree-three component and owns image, cokernel, exactness and injectivity. All targets are planned; inherited source-quotient, Matsumoto and plus-comparison boundaries prevent closure. Nothing is formalised.

nodes.title: Degree-two identification with the classical Matsumoto map
nodes.statement: Let F be a field. Write m_F:K2^M(F)≃K2^cl(F) for the symbol-preserving Matsumoto equivalence, θ1_F for the natural classical-to-Quillen K1 identification, and θ2_F:K2^cl(F)≃K2(F) for the natural classical-to-Quillen K2 identification, normalized so θ2_F({a,b}_cl)=θ1_F([a])·θ1_F([b]). Then the degree-two component Φ_2 of the imported unital graded product map equals θ2_F composed with m_F. In particular Φ_2 is an isomorphism, natural in unital field homomorphisms. This uses the supplied oriented product-symbol theorem and does not derive it from bilinearity or from Matsumoto alone.
hypotheses: F is a commutative field; every symbol entry is a unit.
The K.7 supplier identifies its actual biexact tensor product with the plus-model product, including the unit-matrix formula and its orientation relative to the chosen θ2.
The imported Matsumoto and plus-comparison nodes retain their recorded proof gaps.
proofSteps: Use units-to-K1 and pi1-plus-construction to identify the ordered two unit classes used by Φ with the unit-matrix loops in the product supplier.

The K.7 supplier computes this product as the chosen classical Steinberg symbol transported by θ2. Weibel IV.1.10.1 specifies the convention; Loday Proposition 2.2.3 supplies a calculation with an explicit inverse under his connecting map. The needed natural comparison between that calculation and K.7’s biexact product is a recorded gap, not an automatic identification of all product models.
Evaluate Φ_2 and θ2 composed with m_F on every two-symbol. The Milnor presentation makes these symbols generate the degree-two additive group, so the homomorphisms agree.
Since m_F and θ2 are equivalences, the degree-two map is an equivalence. Transport naturality from the imported graded map and the two supplied natural equivalences.
acceptance: The equality is on the actual degree-two homomorphism, not merely an abstract isomorphism of its source and target.
At ℚ(t), the external tame-symbol test on {2,t} distinguishes the required orientation from its negative.
Only the Matsumoto presentation plus θ2 and product compatibility imply invertibility; checking relations alone does not.

api.name: milnorToQuillen
api.statement: The unique unital graded ring map Φ_F : K^M_*(F) → K_*(F) taking {u} to ι_F(u), the unit matrix class transported through the natural classical K1 comparison.

api.name: milnorToQuillen_zero
api.statement: On degree zero, n maps to n[F]. Through the canonical K0 model comparison and pinned SplitK0.finrankEquiv this is the identity of ℤ.

api.name: milnorToQuillen_one
api.statement: On degree one Φ_F equals θ1_F composed with the additive version of K1.ofUnits; composing with the field determinant equivalence gives the identity on Additive Fˣ.

api.name: milnorToQuillen_two
api.statement: The degree-two map is θ2_F composed with the classical Matsumoto equivalence, using the stated product-symbol orientation. This API item is promoted to K2SymbolsBrauer:T.2/graded-map-degree-two-identification.

api.name: milnorToQuillen_symbol
api.statement: For an n-tuple of units Φ_F({u1,…,un}) is the ordered product ι_F(u1)…ι_F(un). The empty tuple maps to [F]; an identity entry gives zero.

api.name: milnorToQuillen_map
api.statement: For every unital field homomorphism f:F→E, K_*(f) composed with Φ_F equals Φ_E composed with K^M_*(f), in every degree.

api.name: milnorToQuillen_graded
api.statement: The unital algebra map preserves homogeneous degree n. Multiplication of degree p and degree q classes lands in degree p+q.

api.name: milnorToQuillen_mul
api.statement: Φ_F(xy)=Φ_F(x)Φ_F(y), with degree p+q and the canonical degree transport when x and y are homogeneous.

api.name: milnorToQuillen_unique
api.statement: Unital graded ring maps K^M_*(F)→K_*(F) agreeing on every degree-one unit symbol are equal; their degree-zero maps are fixed by unitality.

api.name: milnorToQuillen_steinberg
api.statement: If a and 1-a are nonzero, ι_F(a)ι_F(1-a)=0. This is obtained from the oriented classical symbol comparison and Steinberg identity before descending the tensor map.

api.name: milnorToQuillen_three_symbol
api.statement: The exported degree-three component sends {a,b,c} to (ι_F(a)ι_F(b))ι_F(c). Associativity identifies the other parenthesization; no permutation is implicit.

tests.name: empty_symbol
tests.statement: Φ_F({})=[F], and its image through the pinned finite-dimensional K0 model has dimension 1. A zero map fails this test.

tests.name: unit_one
tests.statement: ι_F(1)=0 in additive K1, so every positive-degree symbol containing 1 maps to zero. The source identity is multiplicative and must not map to the graded ring unit.

tests.name: rational_unit_two
tests.statement: For F=ℚ, determinant of the classical K1 representative of Φ_1({2}) is 2. This rules out a trivial degree-one map or inversion.

tests.name: steinberg_pair
tests.statement: For a≠0,1, Φ_2({a,1-a})=0; multiplying this relation by symbols on either side still gives zero.

tests.name: oriented_rational_function
tests.statement: External sign test using the T.3 convention: at t=0 in ℚ(t), the tame residue of θ2 inverse applied to Φ_2({2,t}) is 2, while reversing the product or negating θ2 gives 1/2. T.3 is a test consumer, not a prerequisite for constructing Φ.

tests.name: field_map_two
tests.statement: For ℚ→ℚ(t), mapping Φ_1({2}) equals Φ_1 of the mapped unit, and the same square commutes for {2,3}. The functor laws hold for identity and composite field maps.

tests.name: triple_one_and_steinberg
tests.statement: Φ_3({a,b,1})=0 and Φ_3({a,1-a,b})=0 whenever the entries exist; the ordered triple formula gives these vanishing statements without V.2.

tests.name: rational_degree_three_not_surjective
tests.statement: External computation: K3^M(ℚ)=ℤ/2 and K3(ℚ)=ℤ/48. The canonical degree-three map is injective by the theorem owned in V.2, hence not surjective. Neither computation nor injectivity is an input to constructing the map.

proofClarifications: Send a unit u to its unit-matrix K1 class, transported by θ1. Extend the resulting integer-linear map through TensorAlgebra.lift.

Use the requested oriented product-symbol compatibility and the imported Steinberg identity to kill every degree-two generator of the two-sided Steinberg ideal. Descend through RingQuot.liftAlgHom; homogeneous degree preservation uses the source grading, not RingQuot alone.
The source’s universal property gives uniqueness, its degree-zero unit and symbol concatenation give multiplicativity, and naturality follows by uniqueness or generator evaluation.
The supplier chain for the actual Quillen ring is K.7/products-from-biexact-functors and its S-grid, stabilization and coherence nodes; no products are constructed here.

gaps.title: G-Matsumoto (inherited)
gaps.detail: The imported Matsumoto node states the presentation but does not decompose its converse normal-form proof. The field-symbol owner must supply that proof; the graded comparison has not proved injectivity just by checking relations.

gaps.title: G-cover-Hurewicz (inherited)
gaps.detail: The natural equivalence of classical K2 with plus-model π2 still has a supplier boundary in T.1/k2-pi2. This continuation does not choose a replacement θ2 solely to force the desired product equality; the existing comparison’s orientation must be established.

gaps.title: G-product-symbol (refined)
gaps.detail: Weibel IV.1.10–1.10.1 and the actual proof of Loday Proposition 2.2.3 have been read, removing the parent’s unread-source requirement. The generic K.7 product node has no map-level theorem identifying its tensor pairing with this plus-model calculation. That model comparison and the connecting-map sign relative to the chosen θ2 remain requested; both the descent proof and degree-two identification require them.

sourceIssues.locator: Combined author draft, III.5.12 introductory paragraph and III.5.12.1 proof, printed p.227 / PDF p.235; inspected the rendered page.
sourceIssues.printed: The free tensor product R^m⊗R^n and its endomorphism matrix ring are assigned rank m+n in the introductory paragraph; the proof again uses that sum for the free module.
sourceIssues.correction: Use rank mn, and identify the endomorphism ring with M_(mn)(R). The stabilized matrices are the Kronecker tensor matrices on this product-rank free module.
sourceIssues.reason: Already m=n=1 gives a rank-one tensor product, not rank two; the source’s subsequent assertion R=E in this case itself requires rank one. The product-rank basis is indexed by pairs of basis indices.
sourceIssues.known: No accessible correction established; this record is scoped to the combined author copy, with no claim about the published edition.
